correctness.rationale: The exact joint mass is obtained from multinomial prefix counting with full support r..m(r-1)+1 and any positive real weights. Strict factorial-sequence log-concavity is preserved by finite convolutions, proved using a strictly positive adjacent Cauchy–Binet summand for every index. The marked probability ratio factorizes as a product of constants and a ratio of two TP2-convolved truncated exponentials. A second explicit strictly positive Cauchy–Binet minor at every time proves monotone likelihood ratio (including both endpoints); m=2 and equality of weights are treated. A deterministic exact rational independent dynamic program and polynomial enumeration agree on 1,737 profiles; small-word enumeration is a third cross-check. The finite computations are only supplementary evidence, not a substitute for the infinite-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The result asserts a new global strict two-time/two-label determinant inequality for the first quota completion, not simply a waiting-time formula. Full primary examinations of Camarri–Pitman (2000), Camarri (1998), and Aston–Martin (2005) show marginal or general finite-state distribution methods without this likelihood-ratio ordering. Targeted literature, published finding and comparisons with prior mathematical claims located no dominating theorem; uncertainty about inaccessible Anderson–Sobel–Uppuluri (1982) is explicitly retained, so priority is a qualified best-knowledge result.

value.rationale: The first of finitely many types to reach a prescribed occurrence quota is a classical occupancy stopping model, and its winning label is an intrinsically motivated mark. The theorem produces a uniform, sharp and strict marked-time stochastic order for all probabilities and integer quotas r>=2, significantly stronger than a marginal mean comparison; its exact endpoint odds calibrate the rare-winner evidence from observed completion time. No arbitrary finite slice or known-table recomputation is used.
